explanation: Clark is confident in KC at 76%. Vegas leans the same way — KC are a 6.5-point favorite, but the signal Clark keeps coming back to is how KC have been playing. BAL allow 0.02 fewer EPA/play than TB on the season, pressure on 8% of dropbacks. L.Jackson has been one of the league's most efficient passers this season (0.33 EPA/att). The main risk is plain variance — a turnover or a special-teams swing can compress the edge fast.
primary_reason: The betting market lands on BAL too: Vegas made them a 4.5-point favorite — about a 69% implied win probability. Lines quietly fold in injury news, weather, and where the sharp money is going — things a box score can't see. When Clark and Vegas independently arrive at BAL, it's usually the steadiest kind of agreement.
secondary_reason: BAL's defense has been the sturdier of the two, giving up 0.02 fewer EPA/play than TB on the season. A lot of it is pressure — BAL are getting to the quarterback on 8% of dropbacks, the kind of heat that rattles B.Mayfield. If they keep B.Mayfield uncomfortable, TB's scoring drives are the ones that stall out.
risk_factor: The main risk is game-state variance: a turnover, a special-teams breakdown, or an early injury can compress the statistical edge quickly.
flip_scenarios: If BAL loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If TB converts its EPA edge into red-zone touchdowns, the model's lean can flip.

Last three: PHI 3-0, WAS 2-1 (15 pt/gm margin swing). J.Hurts has been an above-average passer this season (0.13 EPA/att). The one thing that could turn it: WAS bring the pass rush that matters here. WAS pressure the quarterback on 13% of dropbacks; per-play EPA allowed is otherwise close.
game_diagnosis.primary_reason: The betting market lands on PHI too: Vegas made them a 4.5-point favorite — about a 70% implied win probability. Lines quietly fold in injury news, weather, and where the sharp money is going — things a box score can't see. When Clark and Vegas independently arrive at PHI, it's usually the steadiest kind of agreement.
game_diagnosis.secondary_reason: PHI come in playing the better football — they're 3-0 over their last three while WAS are 2-1. On top of that, PHI hold roughly 15 points per game of margin separation their way. Form like that tends to carry: healthier rotations, cleaner execution, and more belief in the tight moments.
game_diagnosis.risk_factor: WAS bring the pass rush that matters here. The two defenses have been close on a per-play basis, so WAS's edge is about disruption: they're getting to the quarterback on 13% of dropbacks. That pressure is what tilts the matchup — keeping J.Hurts uncomfortable is how PHI's scoring drives stall out.
flip_scenarios: If PHI loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If WAS converts its EPA edge into red-zone touchdowns, the model's lean can flip.

factor_cards.explanation: The betting market lands on ATL too: Vegas made them a 9.5-point favorite — about a 85% implied win probability. Lines quietly fold in injury news, weather, and where the sharp money is going — things a box score can't see. When Clark and Vegas independently arrive at ATL, it's usually the steadiest kind of agreement.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Vegas priced ATL as a 9.5-point favorite — roughly a 85% implied win probability.

factor_cards.name: Defensive Edge
factor_cards.headline: NYG bring the pass rush that matters here.
factor_cards.explanation: The two defenses have been close on a per-play basis, so NYG's edge is about disruption: they're getting to the quarterback on 7% of dropbacks. That pressure is what tilts the matchup — keeping K.Cousins uncomfortable is how ATL's scoring drives stall out.
factor_cards.baseline_note: NYG pressure the quarterback on 7% of dropbacks; per-play EPA allowed is otherwise close.

factor_cards.name: Momentum
factor_cards.headline: ATL are the team trending up.
factor_cards.explanation: ATL come in playing the better football — they're 1-2 over their last three while NYG are 0-3. On top of that, ATL hold roughly 4 points per game of margin separation their way. Form like that tends to carry: healthier rotations, cleaner execution, and more belief in the tight moments.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Last three: ATL 1-2, NYG 0-3 (4 pt/gm margin swing).

factor_cards.name: Recent Offense
factor_cards.headline: ATL own the better recent offense.
factor_cards.explanation: Over the last three weeks ATL have been the more efficient offense — averaging +0.04 EPA/play more than NYG and staying on schedule +6% more often. That production is below-average by league standards this season. The edge has tightened lately, but it still favors ATL. Against NYG, expect ATL to move the ball more consistently and lean on that efficiency on early downs.
factor_cards.baseline_note: ATL hold a +0.04 EPA/play edge over NYG across the last three games.

factor_cards.explanation: Indoors, so weather is off the table and passing games can play at full speed.

factor_cards.explanation: PHI come in playing the better football — they're 3-0 over their last three while KC are 2-1. On top of that, PHI hold roughly 25 points per game of margin separation their way. Form like that tends to carry: healthier rotations, cleaner execution, and more belief in the tight moments.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Last three: PHI 3-0, KC 2-1 (25 pt/gm margin swing).

factor_cards.name: Recent Offense
factor_cards.headline: PHI's offense is heating up.
factor_cards.explanation: Over the last three weeks PHI have been the more efficient offense — averaging +0.18 EPA/play more than KC and staying on schedule +7% more often. That production is elite by league standards this season. And the gap has grown over the last few weeks, not shrunk. Against KC, expect PHI to move the ball more consistently and lean on that efficiency on early downs.
factor_cards.baseline_note: PHI's offense is producing +0.15 EPA/play over its last three — elite vs the rest of the league.

factor_cards.name: Game Context
factor_cards.headline: The setting is close to neutral.
factor_cards.explanation: Indoors, so weather is off the table and passing games can play at full speed.
factor_cards.baseline_note: KC 0d rest · indoors

completed_games_only.rule: Only games before the predicted week are included in the training window.

no_future_leakage.training_rule: Train on seasons before 2024 plus 2024 weeks < 22.

learning_module.simple_explanation: Measures how much value a team creates every snap.
learning_module.why_predictive: Teams consistently generating positive EPA sustain offense better and do not need fluky field position.

explanation_summary: Clark leans KC at 60%. Vegas leans the same way — KC are a 1.5-point favorite, but the signal Clark keeps coming back to is KC's defense. KC pressure the quarterback on 12% of dropbacks; per-play EPA allowed is otherwise close. P.Mahomes has been an above-average passer this season (0.10 EPA/att). The one thing that could turn it: PHI are the team trending up. Last three: PHI 3-0, KC 2-1 (25 pt/gm margin swing).

model_meta.evaluation_method: Expanding-window weekly validation — trained on all prior weeks, predicted each week forward
feature_categories: QB EPA per play (season + last 3 games)
model_meta.market_note: Vegas spread and moneyline are included as model inputs because they encode information the model can't fully capture from box-score stats alone. However, all explanations prioritize football factors over market signals.

current_season_ready_note: This version runs on historical backtest data. During a live season, the same pipeline refreshes weekly using current nflfastR/nflverse data — only games already played are used to build features.
